questions.question: You’re at a party and your friend accidentally spills their drink on your new jacket. What would be the most appropriate response if you wanted to apologise politely?
options: Don’t worry about it! It’s not my fault.
I’m really sorry about this. It’s not my fault at all.
You should have been more careful!
This is your problem, not mine.
questions.answer: I’m really sorry about this. It’s not my fault at all.

questions.question: Your colleague suggests you should start learning Spanish to improve your job prospects. How would you respond if you wanted to politely agree but also express some hesitation?
options: Yes, that’s a great idea! I’ll start tomorrow.
That’s a good suggestion, but I’m not sure I have time right now.
No, I don’t think I need to learn Spanish for my job.
You’re wrong; I already speak Spanish fluently.
questions.answer: That’s a good suggestion, but I’m not sure I have time right now.

questions.question: A customer in a café asks you if you can recommend a good book to read over the summer. What would be the most appropriate way to suggest something?
options: I don’t know anything about books. Maybe you should ask someone else.
Oh, you should read ‘The Great Gatsby’—it’s amazing!
I’m not a book expert, but ‘The Hobbit’ is a classic you might enjoy.
No, don’t waste your time on books; you’ll never finish them.
questions.answer: I’m not a book expert, but ‘The Hobbit’ is a classic you might enjoy.

questions.question: Your friend suggests that you should visit London next weekend, but you have plans. How would you politely decline and offer an alternative?
options: No, I can’t go. I have other plans.
London? That sounds fun, but I can’t make it this weekend.
You’re right; I’ll go with you next time.
London is boring; I’d rather stay home.
questions.answer: London? That sounds fun, but I can’t make it this weekend.

questions.question: You’re at a formal dinner and someone asks if you’d like dessert. What would be the most appropriate way to politely decline?
options: No, thank you. I’m full.
I’m not hungry, so no, thank you.
I’m not allowed to eat dessert at work.
You’re too kind; I’ll have some later.
